solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Up north, temporarily plant peace tree of old

parts.note: sh is a call for quiet, a request for peace
an obsolete spelling of yew, the evergreen tree

explanation.surface: A northern gardener heels in a seedling for now and plants an ancient tree for peace.
explanation.walkthrough: Up north flags a Scots word: to sheugh a plant is to lay it in a trench for a while before planting it properly.
explanation.definitionFit: Scots usage gives this verb the sense of heeling in seedlings, setting them in a trench as a stopgap before final planting.

clue.text: Loon coming from SA direct to South Carolina

parts.note: the US postal abbreviation for South Carolina
to helm is to steer or direct

explanation.surface: Someone from South Africa is sent straight to South Carolina.
explanation.walkthrough: A loon here is a rogue or scamp, not the bird; the word came into English through South African Dutch.
explanation.definitionFit: Loon in its old sense of rascal or worthless fellow matches this South African word for a rogue or scoundrel.

clue.text: Height divine for the Scots climbing a lot

parts.note: H is the standard abbreviation for height

indicators.note: in a down entry, climbing means the letters run upwards, so they are read from the bottom

parts.note: spae is the Scots verb meaning to foretell or divine

explanation.surface: A Scottish clergyman at great height is climbing a long way.
explanation.walkthrough: Divine looks like a noun for a clergyman, but here it is the verb to predict.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, a large quantity of something is described as piles or loads of it, and this plural is the casual word.

clue.text: Unusual tone on photo developed in the usual place

indicators.note: something unusual is out of its normal form, so the letters of the word next to it are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
a developed photo is a pic, informal for picture

explanation.surface: A photographer notices an odd tone on a print as it develops.
explanation.walkthrough: The darkroom picture hides a medical term: the clue's last words are the definition, not more photography.
explanation.definitionFit: A medical term for an organ or tissue sitting in its normal anatomical position, the opposite of ectopic.

clue.text: Two notes above second octave

parts.note: ut is the old sol-fa name for doh, and A is a note of the scale
S is the abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: A singer reaches two notes above the second octave.
explanation.walkthrough: Octave is not musical here: in the church calendar it is the eighth day after a festival, a sense the musical surface hides.
explanation.definitionFit: In church usage an octave is the eighth day after a feast, or the eight days of celebration, which this old word names.

clue.text: Royal Mile beggar developing brazen guile

indicators.note: developing suggests the following words growing into a new shape, so their letters are rearranged

parts.note: the eleven letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A beggar on Edinburgh's Royal Mile is growing ever bolder in his trickery.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Mile is the main street of Edinburgh's old town, so it signals a Scottish word.
explanation.definitionFit: This Scots word means a wandering licensed beggar, so it fits a mendicant working an Edinburgh street.

clue.text: Country with a Polish president

parts.note: a country of the United Kingdom
the article taken as written; with simply joins it on

explanation.surface: A country is paired with a president from Poland.
explanation.walkthrough: Lech Wałęsa led the Solidarity trade union and was President of Poland from 1990 to 1995.
explanation.definitionFit: Lech Wałęsa, founder of Solidarity, became head of state of Poland after the fall of communism.

clue.text: Knows traditionally rain comes around extreme end of March

indicators.note: one word comes around another, so it wraps it on both sides

parts.note: wet weather, rain
OTT is short for over the top, extreme

indicators.note: end of means only the final letter of the following word is kept

parts.note: the last letter of March

explanation.surface: Tradition says rain comes in at the end of March.
explanation.walkthrough: W(OTT)ET + H. Wot is the archaic verb to know, and -eth the old third-person ending.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic form of the verb meaning to be aware of, the old third-person singular of wit or wot.

clue.text: Latvian concerned with line from abroad

parts.note: a Lett is a Latvian
re means concerning, about

explanation.surface: A Latvian is worried about a line from a foreign country.
explanation.walkthrough: A line is a short letter, as in drop me a line; from abroad asks for the French word.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the French word for a letter, and a line is an informal English name for a short written message.

clue.text: Lower parts I learned once with European soprano transposed upwards

indicators.note: in a down entry, moved upwards means the two letters swap round and are read from the bottom

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for European
S is the abbreviation for soprano
Spenser's past tense of con, to learn
taken as written

explanation.surface: A singer recalls learning the lower parts once, with a European soprano transposing up.
explanation.walkthrough: The Italian plural names the second parts in music; the European soprano pair goes to the top, flipped.
explanation.definitionFit: In music these are the second or subordinate parts in a duet or ensemble, lying below the leading part.

clue.text: Relieve old generation without support

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one word sits around the other

parts.note: an age is a generation
a leg supports a table or a body

explanation.surface: The old generation must manage with no support.
explanation.walkthrough: Without looks like it means lacking, but here it means outside. The verb is Spenserian, a form of allege meaning to lighten.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic Spenserian verb meaning to ease or alleviate, flagged by old in the clue.

clue.text: Desperately covet an old piece of Portugal

indicators.note: acting desperately means acting wildly, so the following letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: the seven letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A collector desperately wants an antique Portuguese coin.
explanation.definitionFit: A coin worth a hundredth of the Portuguese escudo, now superseded by the euro, hence an old piece.

clue.text: Counter simply is too short

indicators.note: a word that is too short has lost its tail, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: merely means simply, only

explanation.surface: Someone complains that a shop counter is just too low.
explanation.walkthrough: Counter is not a shop fitting but a playing piece in the old board game of merels, or nine men's morris.
explanation.definitionFit: A playing piece used in the board game merels, also called nine men's morris, so a game token.

clue.text: Molly perhaps eating a weight of fruit

indicators.note: one who eats takes something inside, so the following words go within the first

parts.note: Molly Malone, the Dublin fishmonger of the song
taken as written
a kat is an ancient Egyptian unit of weight
O is a shortening of of, as in o'clock

explanation.surface: Molly, perhaps, is eating a heavy amount of fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: Molly Malone is the cockle-seller of the Dublin song. The answer is an old form of melocoton, a peach grafted on quince.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word for a kind of peach grafted on a quince stock, so a sort of orchard produce.

clue.text: Chauffeur carries rag, part of a long-standing arrangement?

indicators.note: one who carries something holds it within, so the next word goes inside the first

parts.note: a sice or syce, in India a groom or driver
tat is a rag or shabby stuff

explanation.surface: A chauffeur keeps a cloth in the car, part of a longstanding deal.
explanation.walkthrough: A long-standing arrangement is a dried-flower display, which lasts for ages; the question mark flags the play.
explanation.definitionFit: Sea lavender keeps its colour when dried, so it is a staple flower in dried displays that last for years.

clue.text: Attitudes to English heroic poems

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for English
a pose is an attitude, a stance

explanation.surface: An English poet strikes heroic attitudes.
explanation.walkthrough: Attitudes to English sounds like opinions, but to means joined on, so the abbreviation goes at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: An epos is an epic, a long narrative poem about heroes, and this is its plural.

clue.text: Old walk right over — walk wearily

indicators.note: turned over means the letters run the other way, read back to front

parts.note: go in its obsolete sense of walk on foot
RT is an abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: An old walk goes right over, and someone trudges along exhausted.
explanation.walkthrough: Old flags that go is meant in its obsolete sense of walking, as opposed to riding.
explanation.definitionFit: A colloquial verb for trudging along slowly and tiredly, plodding on foot.

clue.text: Making savings including drive mechanism in train?

indicators.note: including means taking something inside, so one word is placed within the other

parts.note: sparing is being thrifty, saving
a drive is an urge, an impulse

explanation.surface: A railway is cutting costs, including on a mechanism in the train.
explanation.walkthrough: Train is not a railway train but a gear train, a series of meshing wheels; the question mark signals the twist.
explanation.definitionFit: Toothed cylindrical wheels meshing in series form a gear train, the usual set of cogs in machines.

clue.text: Jersey postal system collection

parts.note: the mail is the postal system
a lot is a collection, as at an auction

explanation.surface: The postal system on the island of Jersey has a collection.
explanation.walkthrough: Jersey is a Channel Island in the surface, but here it is a garment.
explanation.definitionFit: The French word for a knitted top, as in the yellow one worn by the Tour de France leader, also a swimsuit.

clue.text: A great deal unfinished around theatre raised danger for actors

indicators.note: around means wrapping the word outside the other
unfinished means the last letter is lopped off the word before it

parts.note: taken as written
a pile is a great deal, a lot

indicators.note: in a down entry, raised means the letters are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: rep is repertory theatre

explanation.surface: Raising most of the scenery around a theatre is a hazard for actors.
explanation.walkthrough: A + P(PER)IL. The word appears in Shakespeare's Timon of Athens, so it is danger for actors because it is a stage word.
explanation.definitionFit: A Shakespearean word for peril, found only in a play, so the risk belongs to the theatre.

clue.text: Gem quality men I see ultimately fancy, but no fine one

indicators.note: but no means except for, so the letters named after it are taken out

parts.note: OR is other ranks, ordinary soldiers
taken as written

indicators.note: ultimately means at the very end, so only the final letter of the word before is kept

parts.note: the final letter of see
taken as written, before two letters are removed
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
a means one

explanation.surface: Men admire a jewel's quality, though they find none of it particularly fine.
explanation.walkthrough: FANCY loses F and A to leave NCY. Orient is the lustre of a fine pearl.
explanation.definitionFit: The orient of a pearl is its lustre, and this noun names that brilliant sheen as a quality of a gem.

clue.text: Local press in US clear it with church

parts.note: the American spelling of through, clear or finished
't is a contraction of it, as in 'tis
CH is the abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: Regional newspapers in America clear a story with the church.
explanation.walkthrough: Local press looks like a newspaper but is a dialect verb meaning to push or squeeze.
explanation.definitionFit: A northern English dialect verb meaning to push, squeeze or thrust, so local signals the regional word for press.

clue.text: Banned weapon Middle East left out of military exercises

indicators.note: left out of means removed from, so those letters are taken from the phrase that follows

parts.note: war games are military exercises
ME is the abbreviation for the Middle East

explanation.surface: A prohibited weapon from the Middle East was excluded from army manoeuvres.
explanation.definitionFit: Poison gases such as mustard gas used in combat were outlawed by the Geneva Protocol and later treaties.

clue.text: Pliant timber for binding round stripped ends

indicators.note: round means the first piece goes around the other

parts.note: a wale is a horizontal timber used to brace and bind a structure

indicators.note: stripped means the outside letters are peeled away, keeping the middle

parts.note: the middle letters of ends

explanation.surface: Flexible wood is used for tying around the bare ends of something.
explanation.walkthrough: Ends is the word whose outer letters go, not a pointer to the ends of another word.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scots adjective meaning supple, flexible or agile, so it means bendy like a willow wand.

clue.text: Rook hash which has many bones

parts.note: R is the chess abbreviation for rook
hachis is a French-derived word for a hash of chopped meat

explanation.surface: A rook's meal of hash is full of bones.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a bony dish; the definition is a body part.
explanation.definitionFit: The spinal column, or backbone, is made of many vertebrae, so it is the structure with numerous bones.

clue.text: What could be series about retiree?

definitions.text: What could be series about retiree?

indicators.note: about means going around, so one abbreviation is wrapped around the other

parts.note: ser is an abbreviation for series
an OAP is an old-age pensioner, a retiree

explanation.surface: A television series about a pensioner might be a long-running drama.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: a drama serial about an old-timer could well be one of these.
explanation.definitionFit: A colloquial name for a soap opera, a long-running domestic drama serial on television or radio.

clue.text: A pet piranha going wild, such as can cause blood loss?

definitions.text: such as can cause blood loss?

indicators.note: going wild means running out of control, so the letters before it are thrown into a new order

parts.note: the eleven letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A pet piranha running amok might draw blood.
explanation.walkthrough: The piranha is the obvious bloodsucker, but the definition is an insect order that feeds on blood.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the order of insects comprising fleas, which bite and suck blood from mammals and birds.

clue.text: Brit fish, mostly ordinary

indicators.note: mostly means not all, so the final letter of the word before is cut

parts.note: to angle is to fish
O is the abbreviation for ordinary

explanation.surface: A British angler catches a fairly ordinary fish.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun it means an English or British person, especially one living abroad, as in Anglo-Indian.

clue.text: Ditch local environmentalist that's no good

indicators.note: with no good, the abbreviation for good is taken away from the word

parts.note: a Green is an environmentalist
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A local environmentalist is told to give up, being no good.
explanation.walkthrough: Ditch looks like a verb meaning to drop, but it is the noun; local says the word is dialect, from the West Country.
explanation.definitionFit: A dialect word in south-west England for a drainage channel or watercourse, so a regional name for a trench.

clue.text: Ready for Janacek? Knockout sequence of notes at end of Sinfonietta

parts.note: KO is short for knockout
a run is a rapid scale passage

indicators.note: end of means only the final letter of the following word is used

parts.note: the last letter of Sinfonietta

explanation.surface: Is the composer ready? His Sinfonietta ends with a knockout run of notes.
explanation.walkthrough: Ready is slang for cash, as in the readies. Janáček was Czech, so his money is the Czech currency.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the currency of the Czech Republic and formerly Czechoslovakia, the cash a Czech composer would carry.

clue.text: Antelope raised must yield good type of leather

indicators.note: in a down entry, raised means the word is read from the bottom up
to yield is to give up, so the letter named next is surrendered

parts.note: the nagor is a West African reedbuck, a kind of antelope
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: An antelope is reared to provide good leather.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is also an antelope itself, so the wordplay's first word teases a second reading.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft sheepskin tanned with sumac, used in bookbinding, is known by this name.

clue.text: God covered in old red dye round altar decoration

indicators.note: covered in means placed inside, with the next word wrapping around it

parts.note: grain once meant kermes, a red dye
D for Deo or Deus, God, as in DV, Deo volente
O is a round letter

explanation.surface: A god is draped in old red cloth around a church altar.
explanation.walkthrough: Grain is meant in its old sense of scarlet dye from kermes insects, the source of the phrase dyed in the grain.
explanation.definitionFit: A raised step or shelf behind a church altar, on which candles and ornaments stand.

clue.text: I laze about dying fire in ingle?

indicators.note: about suggests moving around, so the letters before it are shuffled into a new order

parts.note: the five letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone lounges by the fireplace as the fire burns down.
explanation.walkthrough: An ingle is a fireside, and the Scots word for a glowing ember belongs at one.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scots word for a hot ember or cinder, the last glowing remains of a hearth fire.

clue.text: Central town on the Broads, a place to eat

parts.note: cen is a dictionary abbreviation for central
Acle is a small town on the Norfolk Broads

explanation.surface: A central town in the Norfolk Broads has a spot to dine.
explanation.walkthrough: The Norfolk Broads are a network of rivers and lakes in eastern England; Acle is a town there.
explanation.definitionFit: The room where the Last Supper was eaten, hence any supper room or dining room.

clue.text: Smooth tranquillity once interrupting weather

indicators.note: to interrupt something is to break into it, so one word goes in the middle of the other

parts.note: sky in its old sense of weather or climate
lee is an obsolete word for calm, tranquillity

explanation.surface: A calm spell breaks into otherwise smooth weather.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic variant of sleek, meaning glossy and slick, so it is an adjective meaning silky.

clue.text: Address in Portuguese senate hours before

parts.note: sen is the abbreviation for senate
H is the abbreviation for hours
or is an archaic word meaning before, as in or ever

explanation.surface: A Portuguese senate sits for some hours before an address.
explanation.walkthrough: Address is a form of address, a title, not a speech or a street location.
explanation.definitionFit: The Portuguese courtesy title for a man, the equivalent of mister or sir, used when speaking to him.
